1_Aloevera.medicinal_uses: Fresh pulp is a cooling laxative, hepatoprotective and skin-healing agent. Applied topically on burns, wounds and inflammatory skin lesions.
1_Aloevera.dosage_and_formulation: Kumaryasava, Kumari Asava, Aloe Gel, Kanyasara. Prescribed Dosage: 10-20 ml (Juice).
1_Aloevera.precautions: Latex is a strong purgative; avoid in pregnancy, menstruation and bleeding piles.

2_Amla.medicinal_uses: Premier Rasayana rich in vitamin C. Improves immunity, digestion, eyesight and hair health and has antioxidant activity.
2_Amla.dosage_and_formulation: Chyawanprash, Triphala Churna, Amalakyadi Churna, Amalaki Rasayana. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
2_Amla.precautions: Generally safe; high doses may aggravate cold or cause loose stools.

3_Amruthaballi.medicinal_uses: Immunomodulator and antipyretic Rasayana. Used for recurrent fevers, gout and metabolic disorders.
3_Amruthaballi.dosage_and_formulation: Guduchi Satva, Amritarishta, Guduchyadi Kashaya, Giloy Ghan Vati. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
3_Amruthaballi.precautions: Avoid in autoimmune disease without supervision; may lower blood sugar.

4_Arali.medicinal_uses: Bark decoction is astringent and wound healing. Fruits act as mild laxative and respiratory tonic.
4_Arali.dosage_and_formulation: Ashvatthadi Kwatha, Nyagrodhadi Churna, Panchavalkala Kashaya. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.

5_Astma_weed.medicinal_uses: Traditional bronchodilator and antispasmodic. Used for bronchial asthma and amoebic dysentery.
5_Astma_weed.dosage_and_formulation: Dugdhika Churna, Dudhi Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: 1-3 gm.
5_Astma_weed.precautions: Latex irritates eyes and skin; avoid high doses and during pregnancy.

6_Badipala.medicinal_uses: Leaf and bark used for psoriasis and chronic skin lesions. Seeds used as an astringent in diarrhea. (Class name needs botanical verification.)
6_Badipala.dosage_and_formulation: Kutajarishta, Kutaja Churna, Pala Taila. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
6_Badipala.precautions: Use under supervision; avoid in pregnancy.

7_Balloon_Vine.medicinal_uses: Anti-inflammatory vatahara herb. Leaf poultice and decoction used for stiff, painful joints.
7_Balloon_Vine.dosage_and_formulation: Karnasphota Taila, Mudakathan Kashaya. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
7_Balloon_Vine.precautions: Safe in moderate doses; avoid in pregnancy.

8_Bamboo.medicinal_uses: Vamshalochana is a cooling respiratory tonic and bone strengthener. Leaves are used for fever and uterine complaints.
8_Bamboo.dosage_and_formulation: Vamshalochana Churna, Talisadi Churna, Chyawanprash. Prescribed Dosage: 1-3 gm.

9_Beans.medicinal_uses: Nutritive legume. Pod decoction traditionally used as diuretic and to support blood sugar control.
9_Beans.dosage_and_formulation: Pod decoction, Dietary preparation. Prescribed Dosage: 10-30 gm (Food).
9_Beans.precautions: Must be cooked well; raw beans contain toxic lectins. May aggravate Vata.

10_Betel.medicinal_uses: Carminative, expectorant and antimicrobial leaf. Chewed after meals to freshen breath and aid digestion.
10_Betel.dosage_and_formulation: Tambula Swarasa, Nagavalli Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 1-2 leaves.
10_Betel.precautions: Excess use may cause acidity; avoid with tobacco or areca nut chewing.

11_Bhrami.medicinal_uses: Foremost Medhya Rasayana (nootropic). Supports memory, learning and calms the nervous system.
11_Bhrami.dosage_and_formulation: Brahmi Ghrita, Saraswatarishta, Brahmi Vati, Brahmi Taila. Prescribed Dosage: 10-20 ml (Juice).
11_Bhrami.precautions: May cause mild nausea on an empty stomach; best taken with ghee or honey.

12_Bringaraja.medicinal_uses: Rasayana for hair and liver (Keshya, Yakrit-uttejaka). Leaf juice oil is applied for hair growth.
12_Bringaraja.dosage_and_formulation: Bhringarajasava, Bhringaraj Taila, Bhringarajadi Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
12_Bringaraja.precautions: Safe; use caution in very high Pitta.

13_Caricature.medicinal_uses: Leaf decoction used traditionally for hemorrhoids and wounds, with anti-inflammatory action.
13_Caricature.dosage_and_formulation: Leaf decoction, Leaf poultice. Prescribed Dosage: 3-5 gm.
13_Caricature.precautions: Limited classical data; use under guidance.

14_Castor.medicinal_uses: Premier Vata-pacifying purgative oil. Leaf and root used in joint pain and sciatica.
14_Castor.dosage_and_formulation: Eranda Taila, Erandapaka, Gandharvahastadi Kashaya, Rasnaerandadi Kashaya. Prescribed Dosage: 5-10 ml (Oil).
14_Castor.precautions: Seeds contain toxic ricin; never chew raw seeds. Avoid in pregnancy and diarrhea.

15_Catharanthus.medicinal_uses: Source of vinca alkaloids used in oncology. Traditionally leaf extracts are used for diabetes.
15_Catharanthus.dosage_and_formulation: Leaf juice, Decoction. Prescribed Dosage: Leaf juice 5-10 ml.
15_Catharanthus.precautions: Toxic alkaloids; use only under medical supervision; avoid in pregnancy.

16_Chakte.medicinal_uses: Leaf paste applied for ringworm and fungal skin conditions. Seeds mildly laxative. (Class name needs botanical verification.)
16_Chakte.dosage_and_formulation: Chakramardadi Lepa, Dadrughna Vati. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
16_Chakte.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy; excess causes loose stools.

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_karma: Aggravates Pitta, pacifies Kapha and Vata

17_Chilly.medicinal_uses: Digestive stimulant and rubefacient. Capsaicin is used topically for pain relief.
17_Chilly.dosage_and_formulation: Capsaicin ointment, Dietary use. Prescribed Dosage: 0.5-1 gm.
17_Chilly.precautions: Avoid in ulcers, gastritis and high Pitta; irritant to eyes and mucosa.

18_Citron_lime_(herelikai).medicinal_uses: Aromatic digestive and carminative. Rind and juice used for nausea and loss of appetite.
18_Citron_lime_(herelikai).dosage_and_formulation: Jambira Pana, Matulunga Kalpa, Hingvadi Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm (Rind).
18_Citron_lime_(herelikai).precautions: Excess may cause acidity; avoid in high Pitta.

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_karma: Pacifies Kapha, aggravates Pitta and Vata

19_Coffee.medicinal_uses: CNS stimulant and mild diuretic. Chlorogenic acids give antioxidant activity.
19_Coffee.dosage_and_formulation: Beverage, Coffee extract. Prescribed Dosage: 1-2 cups (Beverage).
19_Coffee.precautions: Avoid excess; may cause insomnia, palpitations, acidity and anxiety; limit in pregnancy.

20_Common_rue(naagdalli).medicinal_uses: Antispasmodic and emmenagogue herb. Leaf infusion used for colic and delayed menses.
20_Common_rue(naagdalli).dosage_and_formulation: Sadapa Arka, Leaf infusion. Prescribed Dosage: 1-2 gm.
20_Common_rue(naagdalli).precautions: Abortifacient; contraindicated in pregnancy; phototoxic on skin; toxic in high doses.

21_Coriender.medicinal_uses: Carminative, diuretic and cooling digestive. Cold infusion of seeds soothes burning sensations.
21_Coriender.dosage_and_formulation: Dhanyakadi Hima, Dhanyaka Panchaka Kwatha, Panchakola Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
21_Coriender.precautions: Safe as food and in classical doses.

22_Curry.medicinal_uses: Aromatic digestive and antidiabetic leaf. Supports hair pigmentation and liver function.
22_Curry.dosage_and_formulation: Kaidaryadi Churna, Curry Leaf Chutney. Prescribed Dosage: 5-10 leaves.

23_Doddpathre.medicinal_uses: Leaf juice is a classical remedy for cough, cold and colic in children. Also used for urinary stones.
23_Doddpathre.dosage_and_formulation: Leaf juice, Parnayavani Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: 10-15 ml (Juice).
23_Doddpathre.precautions: Safe in moderate doses; excessive amounts may increase Pitta.

24_Drumstick.medicinal_uses: Nutrient-dense, anti-inflammatory tree. Leaves support lactation and anemia; root is a stimulant.
24_Drumstick.dosage_and_formulation: Shigru Kwatha, Shigru Churna, Moringa Leaf Powder. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
24_Drumstick.precautions: Root bark may cause uterine stimulation; avoid in pregnancy.

25_Ekka.medicinal_uses: Flowers used for chronic respiratory conditions. Leaf fomentation relieves arthritic swelling.
25_Ekka.dosage_and_formulation: Arkadi Kashaya, Arka Taila, Shweta Arka Bhasma. Prescribed Dosage: 0.5-1 gm.
25_Ekka.precautions: Latex is caustic and toxic; avoid eye contact; use only purified preparations.

26_Eucalyptus.medicinal_uses: Decongestant and expectorant. Steam inhalation of leaf oil opens airways.
26_Eucalyptus.dosage_and_formulation: Eucalyptus Taila, Nilgiri Thailam, Inhalation preparations. Prescribed Dosage: 1-2 drops (Oil, inhaled).
26_Eucalyptus.precautions: Oil is toxic if ingested; avoid in infants' faces; dilute before topical use.

27_Ganigale.medicinal_uses: Used only externally as oil or paste for chronic skin lesions. (Class name needs botanical verification.)
27_Ganigale.dosage_and_formulation: Karaveeradi Taila, Karaveera Lepa. Prescribed Dosage: Externally only.
27_Ganigale.precautions: HIGHLY TOXIC (cardiac glycosides). Never ingest. Keep away from children and animals.

28_Ganike.medicinal_uses: Astringent haemostatic used for bleeding and loose stools. (Class name needs botanical verification.)
28_Ganike.dosage_and_formulation: Priyangvadi Churna, Priyangvadi Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: 1-3 gm.
28_Ganike.precautions: Limited modern data; use under guidance.

29_Gasagase.medicinal_uses: Seeds are used as food and cooling nutritive paste; capsule latex is a strong analgesic and sedative.
29_Gasagase.dosage_and_formulation: Poppy seed paste, Ahiphenasava. Prescribed Dosage: 1-3 gm (Seed).
29_Gasagase.precautions: Latex alkaloids are narcotic, habit-forming and legally controlled; use only seeds as food.

30_Ginger.medicinal_uses: Universal medicine (Vishwabheshaja). Carminative, anti-nausea and anti-inflammatory.
30_Ginger.dosage_and_formulation: Trikatu Churna, Sitopaladi Churna, Ardraka Khanda, Shunthi Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: 1-3 gm.
30_Ginger.precautions: May aggravate Pitta or bleeding; high doses can irritate stomach.

31_Globe_Amarnath.medicinal_uses: Flower infusion used for cough and bronchitis. Mild diuretic and cooling.
31_Globe_Amarnath.dosage_and_formulation: Flower decoction, Herbal tea. Prescribed Dosage: 3-5 gm.
31_Globe_Amarnath.precautions: Limited classical data; use in moderation.

32_Guava.medicinal_uses: Astringent leaf decoction used for diarrhea and gum problems. Fruit rich in vitamin C.
32_Guava.dosage_and_formulation: Leaf decoction, Guava leaf tea. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm (Leaf).
32_Guava.precautions: Excess unripe fruit may cause constipation.

33_Henna.medicinal_uses: Cooling leaf paste applied for burning sensation, skin disease and hair care.
33_Henna.dosage_and_formulation: Madayantikadi Lepa, Mehndi Taila. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
33_Henna.precautions: Avoid in G6PD deficiency (hemolysis risk); patch test before use.

34_Hibiscus.medicinal_uses: Cooling flower used for menstrual disorders and hair growth. Leaf paste is used as a shampoo.
34_Hibiscus.dosage_and_formulation: Japa Kusuma Taila, Japa Kusuma Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.

35_Honge.medicinal_uses: Seed oil is antimicrobial and applied for scabies and eczema. Leaves used for piles.
35_Honge.dosage_and_formulation: Karanja Taila, Karanjadi Lepa, Panchatikta Ghrita. Prescribed Dosage: 1-3 gm.
35_Honge.precautions: Oil is irritant if ingested; use externally; avoid in pregnancy.

36_Insulin.medicinal_uses: Leaf chewed fresh for blood sugar support. Corosolic acid improves glucose uptake.
36_Insulin.dosage_and_formulation: Fresh leaf, Leaf powder. Prescribed Dosage: 1-2 leaves/day.
36_Insulin.precautions: Monitor blood glucose if combined with antidiabetic drugs.

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_karma: Pacifies Pitta and Vata, aggravates Kapha

37_Jackfruit.medicinal_uses: Ripe fruit is nutritive and cooling; leaf ash and latex used on wounds and ulcers.
37_Jackfruit.dosage_and_formulation: Dietary use, Panasa Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: Dietary.
37_Jackfruit.precautions: Heavy to digest; excess may cause bloating.

38_Jasmine.medicinal_uses: Leaf chewed for mouth ulcers; flower oil is calming and aromatic.
38_Jasmine.dosage_and_formulation: Jatyadi Taila, Jatyadi Ghrita. Prescribed Dosage: 3-5 gm.
38_Jasmine.precautions: Safe topically; avoid essential oil overuse.

39_Kambajala.medicinal_uses: Used in folk medicine for cough and wounds. (Class name needs botanical verification.)
39_Kambajala.dosage_and_formulation: Leaf decoction (folk). Prescribed Dosage: Local use only.

40_Kasambruga.medicinal_uses: Leaf decoction used for cough and bronchial complaints. Seeds are mildly purgative.
40_Kasambruga.dosage_and_formulation: Kasamardaka Kwatha, Kasamardadi Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
40_Kasambruga.precautions: Seeds can be toxic in excess; avoid in pregnancy.

41_Kohlrabi.medicinal_uses: Nutritive vegetable rich in vitamin C and fiber with antioxidant effects.
41_Kohlrabi.precautions: May cause gas; thyroid caution when eaten raw in large quantity.

42_Lantana.medicinal_uses: Leaf decoction and paste used for skin infections and rheumatism.
42_Lantana.dosage_and_formulation: Leaf paste, Leaf decoction. Prescribed Dosage: 2-3 gm.
42_Lantana.precautions: Hepatotoxic to animals; unripe berries are poisonous. Use externally.

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_karma: Pacifies Vata and Kapha, aggravates Pitta

43_Lemon.medicinal_uses: Rich in vitamin C. Juice used as digestive stimulant and antioxidant.
43_Lemon.dosage_and_formulation: Nimbu Swarasa, Nimbukadi Arka, Lemon Honey Water. Prescribed Dosage: 10-15 ml (Juice).
43_Lemon.precautions: Excess may cause acidity and erode tooth enamel.

44_Lemongrass.medicinal_uses: Aromatic carminative herb used as tea for fever, indigestion and stress.
44_Lemongrass.dosage_and_formulation: Lemongrass Kwatha, Bhustrina Taila. Prescribed Dosage: 5-10 gm.
44_Lemongrass.precautions: Safe in moderate doses; avoid essential oil in pregnancy.

45_Malabar_Nut.medicinal_uses: Foremost Ayurvedic bronchodilator and expectorant. Vasicine acts on bronchial smooth muscle.
45_Malabar_Nut.dosage_and_formulation: Vasavaleha, Vasarishta, Vasakasava, Vasa Swarasa. Prescribed Dosage: 10-20 ml (Juice).
45_Malabar_Nut.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy (uterine stimulant); large doses may cause nausea.

46_Malabar_Spinach.medicinal_uses: Cooling mucilaginous leafy vegetable that is laxative and nutritive.
46_Malabar_Spinach.dosage_and_formulation: Dietary use, Leaf juice. Prescribed Dosage: Dietary.

47_Mango.medicinal_uses: Ripe fruit is nutritive and tonic; seed kernel and bark astringent for diarrhea and bleeding.
47_Mango.dosage_and_formulation: Amrasara, Amra Kwatha, Amra Ghrita. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
47_Mango.precautions: Excess ripe fruit may raise Kapha and blood sugar.

48_Marigold.medicinal_uses: Flower and leaf juice used for wounds, earache and bleeding piles. Lutein supports eye health.
48_Marigold.dosage_and_formulation: Marigold Taila, Flower juice. Prescribed Dosage: 3-5 gm.
48_Marigold.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy; allergy possible in Asteraceae-sensitive people.

49_Mint.medicinal_uses: Carminative, antispasmodic and refreshing digestive herb.
49_Mint.dosage_and_formulation: Pudina Arka, Pudina Satva, Pudinahara Vati. Prescribed Dosage: 5-10 ml (Juice).
49_Mint.precautions: Avoid menthol oil near infants' face; may aggravate reflux.

50_Neem.medicinal_uses: Premier blood purifier and antimicrobial. Leaf paste and decoction used for chronic skin disorders.
50_Neem.dosage_and_formulation: Nimbadi Churna, Nimbadi Kashaya, Panchatikta Ghrita, Neem Taila. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
50_Neem.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy and when trying to conceive; seed oil is toxic to infants.

51_Nelavembu.medicinal_uses: Antipyretic and hepatoprotective bitter tonic widely used for viral fevers.
51_Nelavembu.dosage_and_formulation: Nilavembu Kudineer, Kalmeghasava, Kalmegh Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 1-3 gm.
51_Nelavembu.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy and low blood pressure; very bitter.

52_Nerale.medicinal_uses: Seed powder is a classical antidiabetic that lowers blood sugar and urine sugar.
52_Nerale.dosage_and_formulation: Jambvasava, Jambu Beeja Churna, Jambu Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm (Seed).
52_Nerale.precautions: Monitor blood sugar if on antidiabetic drugs.

53_Nooni.medicinal_uses: Fruit juice used as health tonic; leaf poultice applied to joints and wounds.
53_Nooni.dosage_and_formulation: Noni Juice, Ach Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 10-30 ml (Juice).
53_Nooni.precautions: Avoid in kidney disease and high potassium; liver caution reported.

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_karma: Pacifies Vata, aggravates Pitta and Kapha

54_Onion.medicinal_uses: Raw juice is expectorant and digestive; used for earache and sunstroke.
54_Onion.dosage_and_formulation: Palandu Swarasa, Dietary use. Prescribed Dosage: Dietary.
54_Onion.precautions: Avoid in excess with high Pitta; may cause gas.

55_Padri.medicinal_uses: Root bark is a constituent of Dashamoola; used for fevers and respiratory ailments.
55_Padri.dosage_and_formulation: Dashamoolarishta, Dashamoola Kwatha, Patalarishta. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.

56_Palak(Spinach).medicinal_uses: Iron- and folate-rich leafy green that is mildly laxative and nutritive.
56_Palak(Spinach).dosage_and_formulation: Palak Swarasa, Dietary use. Prescribed Dosage: Dietary.
56_Palak(Spinach).precautions: Avoid in kidney stones (oxalate) and gout when excessive.

57_Papaya.medicinal_uses: Papain aids protein digestion; leaf extract used for platelet support in dengue.
57_Papaya.dosage_and_formulation: Papaya Leaf Juice, Dietary use. Prescribed Dosage: Dietary.
57_Papaya.precautions: Unripe fruit and latex avoided in pregnancy; latex may cause allergy.

58_Parijatha.medicinal_uses: Leaf juice is a classical remedy for fever and sciatica with anti-inflammatory action.
58_Parijatha.dosage_and_formulation: Parijata Kwatha, Parijata Patra Swarasa. Prescribed Dosage: 10-20 ml (Leaf juice).
58_Parijatha.precautions: Safe in moderate doses; may cause mild loose stools.

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_karma: Pacifies Pitta and Kapha, aggravates Vata

59_Pea.medicinal_uses: Nutritive legume; cooked seeds support strength and satiety.
59_Pea.precautions: May cause gas; avoid in Vata aggravation and gout.

60_Pepper.medicinal_uses: Bioavailability enhancer and digestive. Key part of Trikatu and Chaturushana.
60_Pepper.dosage_and_formulation: Trikatu Churna, Sitopaladi Churna, Maricha Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 0.5-1 gm.
60_Pepper.precautions: Avoid in high Pitta, ulcers and acid reflux; may interact with drugs.

61_Pomoegranate.medicinal_uses: Fruit rind is astringent for diarrhea; juice is a heart tonic and hemopoietic.
61_Pomoegranate.dosage_and_formulation: Dadimashtaka Churna, Dadimadi Ghrita, Dadima Swarasa. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm (Rind).
61_Pomoegranate.precautions: Safe; rind in high doses may cause nausea.

62_Pumpkin.medicinal_uses: Cooling nutritive; seeds are traditionally used as anthelmintic.
62_Pumpkin.dosage_and_formulation: Kushmanda Rasayana, Kushmanda Avaleha. Prescribed Dosage: Dietary.
62_Pumpkin.precautions: Heavy to digest; excess may raise Kapha.

63_Raddish.medicinal_uses: Pungent digestive stimulant; juice used for urinary stones and piles.
63_Raddish.dosage_and_formulation: Mulaka Swarasa, Mulaka Kshara. Prescribed Dosage: Dietary.
63_Raddish.precautions: Avoid with high Pitta; raw intake may cause gas; thyroid caution in large amounts.

64_Rose.medicinal_uses: Cooling petals (Gulkand) are mild laxative and heart tonic; rose water used for eyes.
64_Rose.dosage_and_formulation: Gulkand, Gulkand Pak, Gulabarka. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm (Petals).
64_Rose.precautions: Safe; essential oil to be diluted.

65_Sampige.medicinal_uses: Aromatic flowers used for headache and fever; bark for digestive and rheumatic complaints.
65_Sampige.dosage_and_formulation: Champakadi Taila, Champaka Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: 3-5 gm.

66_Sapota.medicinal_uses: Energy-rich fruit; bark used for diarrhea and as a febrifuge.
66_Sapota.dosage_and_formulation: Dietary use, Bark decoction. Prescribed Dosage: Dietary.
66_Sapota.precautions: Excess may increase Kapha; seeds are toxic.

67_Seethaashoka.medicinal_uses: Celebrated uterine tonic. Tones endometrium and arrests abnormal uterine bleeding.
67_Seethaashoka.dosage_and_formulation: Ashokarishta, Ashokaghrita, Ashoka Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
67_Seethaashoka.precautions: Safe in recommended doses; avoid in early pregnancy unless guided by a Vaidya.

68_Seethapala.medicinal_uses: Ripe fruit is a cooling nutritive; leaf paste used for boils and wounds.
68_Seethapala.dosage_and_formulation: Dietary use, Leaf paste. Prescribed Dosage: Dietary.
68_Seethapala.precautions: Seeds are toxic and irritate eyes; avoid in pregnancy.

69_Spinach1.medicinal_uses: Iron-rich leafy green; second image class of Spinacia oleracea (same plant as class 56).
69_Spinach1.precautions: Avoid with kidney stones (oxalate) when excessive.

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_karma: Pacifies Vata, aggravates Pitta and Kapha

70_Tamarind.medicinal_uses: Ripe pulp is mild laxative and digestive; leaf poultice for swellings and wounds.
70_Tamarind.dosage_and_formulation: Tintidika Panaka, Amlikadi Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 5-10 gm.
70_Tamarind.precautions: Excess aggravates Pitta, acidity and joint inflammation.

71_Taro.medicinal_uses: Starchy nutritive tuber; juice from leaves used for wounds.
71_Taro.precautions: Raw plant is acrid due to oxalates; cook thoroughly; avoid in kidney stones.

72_Tecoma.medicinal_uses: Leaf and root decoctions used in folk antidiabetic therapy.
72_Tecoma.dosage_and_formulation: Leaf decoction, Root decoction. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
72_Tecoma.precautions: Monitor blood sugar when combined with antidiabetic drugs; use under guidance.

73_Thumbe.medicinal_uses: Leaf juice used for colds, headache and fever; also used as nasal drops.
73_Thumbe.dosage_and_formulation: Dronapushpi Swarasa, Dronapushpi Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: 10-20 ml (Juice).
73_Thumbe.precautions: Safe in moderate doses; avoid in pregnancy.

74_Tomato.medicinal_uses: Lycopene-rich fruit with antioxidant action and support for skin and heart health.
74_Tomato.precautions: Avoid in acid reflux and gout when excessive; green tomatoes contain tomatine.

75_Tulsi.medicinal_uses: Adaptogenic and immunomodulatory herb. Leaf decoction is the household remedy for cold and fever.
75_Tulsi.dosage_and_formulation: Tulasi Kwatha, Tulasyadi Churna, Sitopaladi Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
75_Tulsi.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy in large doses; may lower blood sugar.

76_Turmeric.medicinal_uses: Anti-inflammatory and antiseptic. Used orally and topically for wounds, arthritis and metabolic disorders.
76_Turmeric.dosage_and_formulation: Haridra Khanda, Haridradi Ghrita, Haridra Churna. Prescribed Dosage: 1-3 gm.
76_Turmeric.precautions: Avoid high doses with gallstones and blood thinners.

77_ashoka.medicinal_uses: Bark and leaf used in folk medicine for fever, hypertension and skin diseases. Often confused with true Ashoka (Saraca asoca).
77_ashoka.precautions: Not a substitute for Saraca asoca; use only under guidance.

78_camphor.medicinal_uses: Topical analgesic, decongestant and antipruritic; inhaled for chest congestion.
78_camphor.dosage_and_formulation: Karpuradi Taila, Karpura Churna, Camphor Balm. Prescribed Dosage: 125-250 mg (crystalline, internal).
78_camphor.precautions: Toxic if ingested in excess; avoid in infants, pregnancy and epilepsy.

79_kamakasturi.medicinal_uses: Aromatic carminative; sabja seeds are cooling and used for heat-related and urinary complaints.
79_kamakasturi.dosage_and_formulation: Sabja Sharbat, Barbari Kwatha. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
79_kamakasturi.precautions: Estragole in essential oil; avoid high doses in pregnancy.

80_kepala.medicinal_uses: Astringent flower and root used for dysentery, menstrual bleeding and sores.
80_kepala.dosage_and_formulation: Flower decoction, Root decoction. Prescribed Dosage: 3-6 gm.
80_kepala.precautions: Limited classical data; use under guidance.

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_karma: Balances Vata and Kapha, promotes Ojas

12_Withania_somnifera.medicinal_uses: Renowned adaptogenic Rasayana herb that reduces cortisol, enhances muscle strength, calms the nervous system, supports restorative sleep, and strengthens cellular vitality.
12_Withania_somnifera.dosage_and_formulation: Ashwagandharishta (15-30 ml), Ashwagandha Churna (3-6 g with warm milk), Ashwagandha Ghrita.
12_Withania_somnifera.precautions: Avoid during pregnancy or hyperthyroidism without professional Ayurvedic supervision.
